presentation.anchor: Gráinne Ní Mháille · Rockfleet · Clew Bay
presentation.question: How could one place hold boats, family, livelihood and authority together?
presentation.opening: Rockfleet stands at the tide line. The chapter treats the castle, inlet, boats and household as one connected system, then keeps the surviving record's limits visible.
presentation.evidenceLimit: Rockfleet's place and later association with Gráinne support a defended maritime base. The walls do not preserve a private family scene or one complete day in the household.
presentation.sourceTitle: Rockfleet place record and the 1593 State Papers
presentation.sourceDetail: Prototype claims C06–C08 · expanded-story review remains open
presentation.artifactPrompt: The chart remains locked until the complete county learning path exists.
presentation.tegCanDo: Recognise and use simple language for place, people and presence in a supported story.

pages.title: A castle where the road is water
pages.body: At Rockfleet, the inlet comes close to the walls. A caisleán here is more than a building set beside a view: it stands where boats can arrive, shelter and leave again.
pages.detail: The chapter begins with geography because the water explains why the place could matter.
pages.visualCaption: Generated editorial interpretation of Clew Bay · not documentary evidence

pages.title: The tide changes the threshold
pages.body: The shore is not a fixed line. Water depth, wind and the turn of the tide change when a boat can approach and where it can wait. That makes local knowledge part of the stronghold.
pages.detail: A castle on this inlet cannot be understood as an isolated tower on dry land.

pages.title: Hear the place before translating it
pages.body: The word belongs to the place you have just entered.

exercise.objective: Recognise caisleán by sound in its Rockfleet context.
exercise.prompt: Listen, then choose the meaning that belongs here.

options.rationale: Long is the word for ship; the sound is different.
Cósta means coast; this word names the building.

exercise.feedback: Caisleán names the castle at the tide line.
exercise.hint: Listen for the broad final sound: cash-lawn.
exercise.recovery: That answer names a different part of the coast. Replay caisleán and try again.

pages.title: Boats extend the walls across the bay
pages.body: The inlet gives the household a defended landing. The boats carry people, goods, news and force beyond it. Castle and fleet do different work, but each makes the other more useful.
pages.detail: That connection is the chapter's first change: Rockfleet becomes a system rather than a landmark.

displayItems.title: Reach

pages.title: The stronghold held people as well as stone
pages.body: A teaghlach is a household or family. The 1593 papers name children and a brother inside Gráinne's political crisis. Mac names a son; bean names a woman. Together they make clear that pressure on one person could reach a wider household.
pages.detail: The documents give these relationships political weight without giving us a private family portrait.

displayItems.title: bean
displayItems.detail: woman · a person in her own right

pages.title: Keep people and place distinct
pages.body: Match each Irish word to the person or place it names.

exercise.objective: Connect the four Rockfleet headwords to their meanings.
exercise.prompt: Choose an Irish word, then the meaning that belongs with it.
exercise.feedback: The household and the stronghold now have separate names.
exercise.hint: Replay the Irish words. Caisleán is the place; the other three name people or relationships.
exercise.recovery: Those two do not belong together. Keep the first word selected and try another meaning.

pages.context: Tá muid go léir · we are all
pages.body: Listen to the whole line before rebuilding it.

exercise.objective: Rebuild a complete Irish sentence from bundled audio.
exercise.prompt: Play the model, then put the words in the order you hear.
exercise.feedback: Tá muid go léir — the whole line stays together.
exercise.hint: The verb Tá opens the sentence.
exercise.recovery: The words are right, but their order changes the line. Replay it and rebuild from Tá.

pages.title: Relationships were part of authority
pages.body: Rockfleet is associated with Gráinne's Bourke marriage and later base. Her authority also depended on relationships that reached beyond one household: followers, neighbouring powers and shifting alliances all mattered.
pages.detail: The surviving record is strongest when it names people inside a dispute. It is weaker as a window into ordinary domestic life.

pages.title: Build the household line
pages.body: Use the new word inside a complete sentence.

exercise.objective: Produce teaghlach inside a complete location sentence.
exercise.feedback: Tá an teaghlach anseo — the household is here.
exercise.hint: Begin with Tá, then name what is here.
exercise.recovery: Every word is useful. Put the verb first, then the household, then anseo.

pages.title: Write the place with its fada
pages.body: Type the full line. The fada is part of the word, not decoration.

exercise.objective: Type a complete sentence with the fada in caisleán.
exercise.feedback: The fada keeps caisleán intact inside the sentence.
exercise.hint: Use the á key twice: Tá … caisleán.
exercise.recovery: The meaning is close. Check the word order and both fadas, then try again.

pages.title: Harbour, household and stronghold worked together
pages.body: The landing makes movement possible. The walls protect a base. The household and followers turn that base into lived authority. Remove one part and the others become less secure.
pages.detail: This is an interpretation built from place, later association and the political relationships visible in the papers—not a recovered floor plan of Gráinne's daily life.

pages.title: Answer from the place in front of you
pages.context: Cad atá anseo? · What is here?
pages.body: Complete the exchange with the line the chapter has earned.

exercise.objective: Use the castle sentence as a relevant dialogue turn.
exercise.prompt: Cad atá anseo? Choose the complete answer.

options.rationale: It answers what is here with a complete sentence.
The words are relevant, but this is not the complete location line.
That says the ship is there, not that the castle is here.

exercise.feedback: The reply names the place and completes the thought.
exercise.hint: Use Tá … anseo to say what is here.
exercise.recovery: That line changes the object or leaves the answer unfinished. Try the complete castle sentence.

pages.title: Rebuild the system
pages.body: Put the chapter's causal chain in order.

exercise.objective: Sequence the relationship between inlet, boats, castle and household.
exercise.prompt: Start with the physical place, then follow what it enables.
exercise.answer: The inlet gives boats a landing. | The castle protects a base. | The household turns the base into lived authority.
tokens: The household turns the base into lived authority.
The inlet gives boats a landing.
exercise.feedback: The sequence begins with place and ends with people using it.
exercise.hint: Begin with the inlet. Water comes before the defended base.
exercise.recovery: The pieces belong to the same system, but cause and consequence have changed places. Start with the inlet.

pages.title: The papers show a political household, not a private scene
pages.body: The State Papers name parents, marriages, children, lands and maintenance because those facts matter to a case before government. The questions shape what becomes visible.
pages.detail: A document made for state business cannot be treated as an intimate account simply because it names family relationships.
pages.visualCaption: TNA SP 63/170 · a surviving state paper, shown as evidence

pages.title: Ask only what the evidence can answer
pages.body: Choose the conclusion supported by the chapter's evidence.

exercise.objective: Distinguish a supported political relationship from an invented domestic scene.
exercise.prompt: Which conclusion stays within the surviving evidence?
exercise.answer: Rockfleet, boats and family relationships were connected parts of Gráinne's authority.

options.text: Rockfleet, boats and family relationships were connected parts of Gráinne's authority.
options.rationale: Place evidence and the political record support the connection when it remains carefully worded.

options.text: The papers describe one ordinary evening inside Rockfleet.
options.rationale: The papers do not preserve a private domestic scene.

options.text: Rockfleet mattered only as an empty defensive tower.
options.rationale: That removes the household, boats and wider relationships the chapter has established.

exercise.feedback: The connection is supportable; the private scene is not.
exercise.hint: Choose the claim that joins place and political relationships without inventing a witnessed day.
exercise.recovery: That conclusion asks the walls or papers to preserve more than they do. Keep the claim at the level of connection.

pages.title: Notice what stays in place
pages.body: The words in the middle can change while the location frame remains useful.

exercise.objective: Discover the reusable Tá … anseo location frame from examples.
exercise.prompt: Tá an caisleán anseo. Tá an teaghlach anseo. What pattern do both lines share?
exercise.answer: Tá + the person or thing + anseo.

options.text: Tá + the person or thing + anseo.
options.rationale: Both lines use Tá to place someone or something here.

options.text: Every noun becomes plural after Tá.
options.rationale: Neither example demonstrates a plural rule.

options.text: Tá marks that the action happened yesterday.
options.rationale: These lines describe what is here, not a past action.

exercise.feedback: Tá … anseo is a small frame you can reuse with a new person or thing.
exercise.hint: Look at the first and last words in both examples.
exercise.recovery: That rule is not present in the examples. Compare what stays unchanged at each end.

pages.title: The walls do not tell a whole life
pages.body: Rockfleet's position helps explain a defended maritime base. Later association and the 1593 papers help connect place, household and authority. They do not let us watch one unrecorded day inside the castle.
pages.detail: Keeping that limit visible makes the supported story stronger, not smaller.

pages.title: Put the household in your own voice
pages.context: Tá muid go léir · we are all
pages.body: Hear the model, record locally, then compare without a score.

exercise.objective: Compare your production of a complete Irish sentence with the bundled model.
exercise.prompt: Listen once. Record when you are ready. No pronunciation score is produced.
exercise.feedback: You made a local recording and compared it with the model. Nothing was graded or uploaded.
exercise.hint: Listen for one continuous line rather than four isolated words.
exercise.recovery: The microphone is optional. You can replay the model and continue without recording.

pages.title: A connected system can be pressured at several points
pages.body: If boats are seized, movement narrows. If kin are held, the household is pressured. If maintenance is cut away, authority becomes harder to sustain. Rockfleet helps make the coming crisis legible.
pages.detail: The next chapter asks what road remains when local power can no longer resolve that pressure.

pages.title: The coast becomes a set of stakes
pages.body: Rockfleet has changed from a picturesque ruin into a place where movement, defence, family and livelihood meet. That makes the later losses concrete: pressure on the coast can reach every part of the system.
pages.detail: The chapter exits with a question rather than a vocabulary summary: what can Gráinne do when those connected supports are threatened together?

pages.title: Bring the place word back
pages.body: Complete the sentence after the story has changed what the castle means.

exercise.objective: Retrieve caisleán later inside a complete sentence.
exercise.prompt: Tá an ___ anseo. Choose the word that completes the line.

options.rationale: The chapter is locating the castle here.
Mac means son and does not name the place in this sentence.
Bean means woman; the sentence is returning to Rockfleet itself.

exercise.feedback: Caisleán returns inside the full location line.
exercise.hint: The blank names Rockfleet as a building.
exercise.recovery: That word names a person. The sentence is locating the stronghold itself.

pages.title: Carry the whole connection forward
pages.body: You can now hear and use caisleán and teaghlach inside more than one task. The language carries the chapter's central relationship: a defended place and the people whose lives and authority gathered around it.
pages.detail: The complete Mayo path will reuse these words again. This chapter proof does not yet turn the county gold.
